title: Preanchored one-hit weld models change shared-window scaling but retain contact and load-survival gates
status_authority: Actual version-bound scoped internal review governs acceptance. Source reports, mathematical verification and physical acquisition remain separate.
reported_status: accepted_internally_verified for the specified one-hit window, independent/shared association-loss and single-end counting arguments; prior two-hit models retain their own acceptance. Actual wet welding remains unacquired and the hybrid optimum has missing governing code.
scientific_scope_status: The earlier symmetric four-arm two-hit shared-window model retains its N^-1/2 tail. A mechanically useful preanchor changes the required operation to one additional old-side graft. With k=d and X=N*a*eta*theta*S, independent thinning under T~Exp(d) gives one-hit no-link failure(1-exp(-X))/X and fixed-m failure asymptotic m/X. This is a changed interface, not a refutation of the two-hit law. Correlated loss of every preanchor in a region imposes a ceiling that abundance cannot remove. A single usable terminus per chain also makes useful sites per mass proportional to a*e*theta*S/M when other kinetic/retention factors are held fixed. Neither a physical weld nor a cost advantage is acquired.
